items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XI, List of Answers on Terminology 75:1
items.html: Aba ve Ima of Atzilut, who are the level of Bina, are always divided into two Partzufim: Aba ve Ima and Israel Saba ve Tevuna — that is, two phases of Aba ve Ima: the upper Aba ve Ima and the lower Aba ve Ima. And at the time of the birth of ZON, the lower Aba ve Ima themselves are also divided into two phases: the first remains at its own level, and the second diminishes to the phase of VAK, in the secret of “crouching.” There are now found three phases of Ima: the upper Ima, the first Tevuna, and the second Tevuna. From this you will understand that this second Tevuna may be called the third Tevuna — that is, in combination with the first, the upper Ima, she is indeed the third to her. But she may also be called the second Tevuna, that is, only according to the name Tevuna, in which the upper Ima is not included, so that accordingly there are here only two Tevunas, the first and the second. Hence it is the ARI's way to call her by the name “the third Tevuna, who is the second,” meaning that she is third to the upper Ima, and second within the phase of Tevuna. (Item 100)
